{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My colleague fell asleep during his night shift and a shipment spoiled. When the warehouse manager demanded answers, I said I'd been the one dozing. I got demoted and a pay cut. He had three kids and was already on final warning. He cried in the parking lot but never corrected me.

CANDIDATE A:
My dog knocked over and shattered my mother-in-law's antique lamp while my wife was home alone. When her mother arrived for dinner and demanded to know what happened, my wife said I'd been roughhousing carelessly. I overheard and said nothing. I absorbed two years of her mother's cold treatment. My wife never corrected the story, and I never asked her to.

CANDIDATE B:
My colleague fell asleep during his night shift and a shipment spoiled. When confronted by the manager, he admitted his mistake immediately. He received a warning and mandatory retraining. Taking responsibility improved his standing with the team over time.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:27"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both involve someone taking the blame for another's mistake, resulting in personal consequences, while the person at fault remains silent and does not correct the false narrative."}
